Each group of three casts one vote, so the total number of votes is C(n,3). If every person has the same number of votes, each gets C(n,3)/n = (n−1)(n−2)/6, which must be an integer.

**Necessary condition.** (n−1)(n−2) is always even, so it is divisible by 6 exactly when it is divisible by 3. That happens when n ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 3), that is, when n is not a multiple of 3.

**Sufficient condition.** Suppose n is not divisible by 3. Label the people by Z_n and let the cyclic shift act on the 3-subsets. A triple fixed by a nontrivial shift would have to be a union of cycles of that shift, which forces 3 to be a multiple of the cycle length, so n would be divisible by 3. Hence every orbit has exactly n triples. In each orbit, pick one triple and have it vote for person 0. Then each shift of that triple votes for the correspondingly shifted person. This gives every person exactly one vote from each orbit, so all vote counts are equal.

**Counting.** The range 10 to 100 contains 91 integers. The multiples of 3 in this range are 12, 15, …, 99, which is (99−12)/3 + 1 = 30 numbers. So there are 91 − 30 = 61 possible values of n.

ANSWER: 61
